title: Length-prefixed JSONL frames for SSE + function-call compatibility
creator: Priya Gupta
description: Implement a dual-mode SSE framing scheme that uses length-prefixed JSONL frames to guarantee tool/function-call atomicity and safe resumability across legacy EventStream and modern ReadableStream clients. This ticket defines the protocol, server-side implementation plan, and rollout/canary steps. The goal is to make reconnects deterministic, prevent partial functioncall deserialization on resume, and provide a straightforward compatibility shim for older clients that expect JSONL sentinel tokens.
background_and_problem_statement: We have recurring customer-reported issues where reconnects during streaming sometimes cause function call payloads or structured outputs to be returned in partially reassembled chunks, leading to JSON parse errors or accidental duplicate tool invocations. Existing approaches in the codebase use sentinel lines (e.g., "","--END--") or naive newline-delimited JSON, which are brittle under multiplexing and proxy reassembly. We need a robust framing scheme that: (1) ensures each high-level event (text delta, function call start/finish, structured record) is atomically resumable, (2) integrates with the SSE transport and our legacy EventStream clients, and (3) minimizes overhead and complexity for the runtime kernel and client SDKs.
proposal_summary: Introduce length-prefixed JSONL frames for streaming events. Each frame begins with an ASCII header specifying a decimal byte length and a small metadata token, e.g., 'L:<bytes>;T:<type>\n', followed immediately by exactly that many bytes of UTF-8 JSON payload. Types include 'delta', 'funcstart', 'funcbody', 'funccall', 'meta', and 'end'. The server emits frames as SSE 'data:' messages. On reconnect, clients present an opaque continuation handle (ledger cursor) pointing to the last fully-received frame id. The server will never consider partial frames committed for resume; partial frames are re-sent in full. For legacy clients, we provide a compatibility flag that emits the sentinel JSONL wrapper (single-line objects with an extra '_compat' field) in addition to length prefixes for a short transitional window.
acceptance_criteria: SSE stream emits frames with ASCII length header followed by exact JSON payload inside each 'data:' event
Server maintains a lightweight per-session ledger (frame ids + offsets) for resume negotiation and can return continuation handles <= 256 bytes
On simulated network cut at random byte offsets, client resumes without JSON parse failures and function-call payloads are delivered exactly once
Backward compatibility mode toggled via client Accept header returns sentinel JSONL copies for older SDKs
Benchmarks show <3% p99 latency increase for typical 2-4 token deltas and <4% bandwidth overhead due to headers on median payloads
API docs and SDK changes merged with tests and integration PRs linked
technical_notes: Key trade-offs considered: (A) length-prefix vs sentinel token; length-prefix guarantees exact reassembly boundaries and simplifies idempotency logic. (B) Binary framing (e.g., WebSocket subprotocol) would be more compact but breaks SSE/Readablestream compatibility. (C) Per-frame ledger increases state but we limit retention by TTL and checkpoint consolidation. The header format chosen is human-readable for debugging but easy to parse in O(1) time. Continuation handles are HMAC'd to prevent client forging and include server epoch + frame_id. We will add a short-lived ledger encryption key rotation and place handles behind a scoped ACL to avoid replay across sessions.
implementation_plan: 1) Spec: finalize header grammar and continuation handle bytes (this ticket)
2) Server: implement frameizer in runtime output layer (C++/Rust module) that emits length-prefixed frames and maintains ephemeral ledger entries

3) Proxy: ensure edge proxies (nginx/gateway) do not split our SSE 'data:' events. Add guard in our edge to buffer until header+payload is complete before flushing. Update stream chunk sizes heuristics.
4) SDKs: add parser utilities for length-prefixed JSONL for Node/Python/Go. SDKs will also implement resume negotiation using continuation handle.
5) Backwards compat: implement Accept: application/sse+jsonl-compat header handling and transitional sentinel emission (server emits both frames and sentinel copies).
6) Tests: unit tests for frameizer, property tests for random cut/resume, integration tests with browser ReadableStream, and e2e tests behind gateways
7) Canary: deploy to canary cluster behind feature flag for 5% of traffic, monitor parse errors, duplicate functions, and p99 latency
8) Ramp: 25% -> 75% -> 100% with fallback window of 72 hours for automated rollback on regressions
progress_updates: 2026-03-01: Ticket created after synthesis of multiple customer incidents and internal bug triage (INC-9921). Initial spec drafted.
2026-03-03: Spike implemented a prototype frameizer in runtime staging branch (branch: feat/frameizer-proto). Observed simple integration with existing SSE emitter.
2026-03-05: Ran property tests simulating random TCP mid-chunk cut. Prototype returned fully-formed JSON on resume in 98/100 trials; failures investigated and fixed (off-by-one length handling).
2026-03-08: Design review with SDK leads (Rafael Ortiz, Mei Lin). Agreed on header grammar and continuation handle HMAC. Added docs requirement for each SDK to surface resume behavior to users.
2026-03-11: Security review kickoff; initial threat model: forged continuation handles, ledger leakage, cross-session replay. Decided on HMAC + expiry + session-scoped salt.

2026-03-13: Runtime PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/872 (frameizer + ledger store). Basic unit tests included. Edge proxy change proposal in infra repo: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1145.
2026-03-13: Canary plan drafted; monitoring dashboards: stream-parse-errors, funccall-duplicates, sse-p99-latency, continuation-handle-failures. Alert thresholds defined.
open_questions_and_decisions: Q: Ledger persistence model — in-memory vs Redis. A: Use an in-memory LRU with optional Redis fallback for multi-node sessions. Decision: start with in-memory per-pod ledger + sticky session routing; evaluate Redis only if canary shows high cross-node resume rates.
Q: How to signal 'end-of-stream' and function-call completion? A: Use explicit 'end' frame type and a terminal 'funccall' frame with 'completed':true. This prevents ambiguous replays.
Q: Cost of dual-emitting sentinel copies for compat. A: Benchmarked; overhead ~6% at median sizes. Decision: enable compat copies only when Accept header requests it (default off).
Q: SDK adoption timeline. A: Node/Python first (two weeks), Go/Java follow-up. Provide JS polyfill to accelerate web adoption.
Q: Rollback strategy. A: Feature-flagged rollout with canary and automated alerts. If funccall duplicates > 0.1% or parse errors spike, rollback to previous emitter immediately.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Edge proxies re-chunk SSE data incorrectly -> Mitigation: buffer until complete header+payload is assembled; add integration test with common proxies.
Risk: Longer headers increase bandwidth for tiny deltas -> Mitigation: micro-optimization: short numeric header when payload < 64 bytes, drop type token for simple delta frames.
Risk: Continued client fragmentation due to old SDKs -> Mitigation: compat mode and outreach to top accounts; include migration guides and code samples.
Risk: Ledger memory growth -> Mitigation: TTL and checkpoint compaction every 30s; metrics to surface ledger size per-pod.
testing_plan: Unit: header parser/serializer property tests, ledger lifecycle
Integration: Node + Browser ReadableStream + nginx proxy + runtime in a loopback environment, simulating random network cuts
E2E: create smoke tests that reproduce past customer incidents and validate no parse errors/duplicate function invocations
Load: benchmarking under 10k concurrent streams to measure p99 latency and bandwidth delta
Security: attempt continuation-handle replay/fake session tests in internal red team
links: Incident: INC-9921 (customer parse failures on resume)
notes_for_reviewers: Focus review on: header grammar clarity, HMAC continuation handle format, and edge buffering strategy. Please comment if the proposed per-pod ledger + sticky sessions is unacceptable for your owned services; we can prioritize a Redis-backed ledger but that increases operational complexity. Also validate the acceptance criteria for perf to ensure metrics are measurable in our observability stack.
